# Elba (01, engineer) — SPD-030

## Brief
Objective: make PreToolUse(Bash)'s reading of wrappers and of the working directory agree with the shell's, so a git write behind an upper-case wrapper is refused (Law 7) and a relative redirection after a directory change the shell never makes, or one the hook cannot follow, is not checked against the wrong directory (Laws 1 and 5). Where the hook and the shell could disagree, the hook errs toward refusing. Red-first.

The hole (proposal from SPUD-029/Clearwater; `spud ticket show SPD-030` has the evidence). On macOS, PATH lookup is case-insensitive (APFS): ENV, NOHUP and CD resolve to /usr/bin/ENV, /usr/bin/NOHUP, /usr/bin/CD, while shell builtins and reserved words are matched exactly. In bin/spud_ledger.py, analyse_segment strips a wrapper only when `os.path.basename(w) in WRAPPERS` (exact case), and strip_wrapper compares the name exactly, so `ENV git commit -m x` and `NOHUP git push` are silent. The command word is then casefolded, so `CD /tmp` and `/usr/bin/cd /tmp` are taken as a change of directory; both run an external cd in its own process, the shell's directory does not move, and `CD /tmp && echo x > ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md` lands in the repository unchecked. pushd and popd are not followed at all (`pushd <home>/ledger && echo x > tickets/SPD-001.md` is silent), and `cd -P /x` or `cd -L /x` takes the option as the directory.

Required:
1. Wrappers are recognised case-insensitively, in the WRAPPERS test and in strip_wrapper's per-name option handling (timeout's duration, sudo/nice/xargs value options, env assignments).
2. Only the exact word `cd` (after wrappers that keep a builtin a builtin) changes the directory. `CD`, `Cd`, `/usr/bin/cd` and cd behind a wrapper that runs an external program (env, nohup, nice, timeout, sudo, xargs, ...) leave it where it was. Decide with evidence which wrappers keep cd a builtin (`command`, `builtin`, and whatever `time` and `exec` do in zsh and bash), and whether an upper-case `COMMAND cd` or `BUILTIN cd` is the builtin (it is not; say what it runs).
3. pushd follows like cd; popd, and pushd with no directory or a stack argument (`+1`, `-1`), leave a directory the hook cannot follow (cwd None).
4. cd or pushd with options: either parse them (`-P`, `-L`, `-e`, `-@`, `-q`, `-s`, `--`) and follow the directory, or treat any option as unfollowable (cwd None). Your call; state which and why.
5. Confirm what cwd None does to a member's and to Spud's relative redirection and tee target (the ticket says refused for a member); pin it with a test.

Check and decide, each with a probe of the real shell (the Bash tool runs the user's shell: zsh on this Mac, bash elsewhere, so decide for both) and a test either way: a cd inside a subshell `(cd /tmp) && echo x > rel`, which must not carry out; a cd in a pipeline element (bash runs every element in a subshell, zsh runs the last one in the current shell); `CDPATH=<dir>` assigned earlier in the line or inherited, which makes a relative cd land under CDPATH; zsh's two-argument `cd old new`; `~user` and `~+`/`~-` targets. Fix those that live in analyse_command/analyse_segment and their helpers. Anything larger, or outside this function family, becomes a proposal (`spud proposal file`), not a fix.

Out of scope: how a script named spud is recognised (spud_launcher, the `base == "spud"` branch) is SPD-032; native permission rules and `spud settings sync` (SPD-033 territory); the database and state-directory refusals (SPD-031, just merged). Do not change them.

Deliverables (only these paths): `bin/**`, `tests/**`. Never `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `ledger/`, `reports/`, `docs/`.

Read first: `spud ticket show SPD-030`; `spud member show SPUD-029/Clearwater` and `spud member show SPUD-031/Linda` (the last two changes to these hooks); in `bin/spud_ledger.py`: `WRAPPERS`, `RESERVED_WORDS`, `ASSIGNMENT_RE`, `shell_tokens`, `separate_redirects`, `strip_wrapper`, `analyse_command`, `analyse_segment` (the `cd` branch), the analysis class that holds `cwd`, `kinds` and `redirects`, `bash_reason`, `edit_reason`; `tests/test_hooks.py` `PreBashTest` and its helpers; `tests/helpers.py`.

Constraints: the hook budget holds: measure PreToolUse(Bash) median of 15 before and after, same payloads (one git write, one redirection after cd, one plain spud call), interleaved with a scratchpad copy of the unchanged bin/, and put both numbers in the result. The live hooks run the ledger root's `bin/spud` on `main`, not this worktree's copy, so your edits do not change enforcement while you work; probe with a scratch SPUD_HOME as the tests do, never against the live ledger. The live Bash hook refuses git writes for you and any command naming the ledger state directory, and the harness refuses shell text naming git that it cannot show stays in the worktree, so build such commands inside Python test code, not in your own shell text. Probing a real cd in the shell is fine in the scratchpad. Run the suite from this worktree in the background: `python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` (450 tests, about two and a half minutes). No Fable today (Eric's budget): any `claude -p` probe passes an explicit `--model haiku`.

## Ticket proposals
- **Bash hook: Spud's relative redirection after a directory the hook cannot follow goes unchecked** — suggested P3; created as [[SPD-035]] at P3 by Spud.
  Why: bash_reason skips a relative redirection or tee target whose directory is unknown (cwd None) when the caller is Spud, so Law 1 and Law 5 do not hold for it; members are refused. SPD-030 narrowed the cases (a directory the shell may or may not be in is now checked for both) but kept this one as it was.
  Evidence: Pinned in tests/test_hooks.py ShellModelTest.test_directories_the_hook_cannot_follow on branch worktree-spd-030-bash-hook-cd-wrappers: for Spud, 'popd; echo x > ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md', 'cd -; ...', 'source x.sh; ...', 'cd $DIR; ...' and a relative cd in a loop are silent; the same with an absolute target is refused (Law 1). Fix sketch: refuse Spud too (his own files are few, so the cost is small), or check the target against the payload cwd as well.
- **Bash hook: a glob in a redirection target writes a file the hook never checks** — suggested P2; created as [[SPD-034]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: bash_reason checks a redirection or tee target as spelled, but zsh and bash -c expand a glob in it (to one match) before opening, so a member or Spud can write a generated ledger file or another member's deliverable through a pattern that matches no rule; Laws 1 and 5.
  Evidence: Probe (zsh 5.9, bash 3.2) in a scratch directory holding ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md: 'echo overwritten > ledg*/tickets/SPD-00?.md' overwrote ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md in zsh and bash, rc 0; /bin/sh (posix mode) refused it. The hook sees the literal path ledg*/tickets/SPD-00?.md, which is under no generated root. Not part of SPD-030's directory following. Fix sketch: a target holding * ? [ or a brace list is expanded with glob against each directory the shell may be in and every match checked, and refused for a member when nothing matches it now.

## Result
**Produced** (worktree spd-030-bash-hook-cd-wrappers, uncommitted): bin/spud_ledger.py and tests/test_hooks.py only.

**The fix.** The Bash hook's working directory is now a set of candidate directories, every one checked, or None when unknown (ShellAnalysis.cwds). A ShellWalk over operator tokens replaces split_segments. It tracks subshells, command and process substitutions, groups, if/case/loop/function frames, and-or lists, pipelines and background jobs. Operator runs such as `)>` and `)&&` are split. Unquoted newlines separate commands (newlines_as_separators; comments keep their words with quotes blanked). Wrappers are matched case-folded, with per-wrapper value options (WRAPPER_VALUE_OPTIONS), and `env -S` and GNU `script -c` strings are analysed. Only exactly spelled cd, chdir, pushd and popd, behind prefixes that keep a builtin in the shell, change the directory.

**Decisions, each with its shell probe** (zsh 5.9 and bash 3.2 run from the scratchpad; `pwd` after):
1. Wrappers casefolded: ENV, NOHUP, COMMAND, TIME, SUDO and XARGS resolve to /usr/bin/* (shutil.which). BUILTIN and EXEC are not found, and stripping them only over-refuses. Added noglob and nocorrect (zsh runs `noglob /bin/echo`) and zsh's `-` precommand (`true; - /bin/echo` runs in zsh).
2. Directory never moves: CD, Cd, /usr/bin/cd, env/nohup/nice/timeout/sudo/xargs cd, COMMAND cd (runs /usr/bin/COMMAND, a sh script), BUILTIN cd (not found), TIME cd, exec cd, coproc cd. Probe: pwd unchanged in both shells. Moves in both: cd, builtin cd, time cd, FOO=1 cd, ! cd, { cd; }, eval 'cd'.
3. Moves in one shell only, so both directories are checked: `command cd` and `command -p cd` (bash moves; zsh runs the external and stays; this differs from the brief's expectation that command cd is followed); noglob/nocorrect/`-` cd and chdir (zsh only); `time -p cd` (zsh runs -p as a command); `builtin command cd`, `command builtin cd`.
4. pushd dir and `pushd -- dir` follow like cd. popd, popd -n, pushd with no directory or +N/-N, and pushd with any other option are unfollowable (None). Probe: `pushd -q` and `-L`/`-P` work in zsh only; bash 3.2 rejects them.
5. cd options: parsed, not blanket None. -L, -P, -LP and -- are read alike by both shells (probe: `cd -P link/..` lands in the link target's parent in both; -L stays logical). -P resolves with realpath. Every other option (-q -s -e -@ -x -N +N) is None: zsh reads an unknown option as the first string of `cd old new` (probe: `cd -e /tmp` tried to substitute "-e" in PWD), and bash 3.2 rejects it.
6. cwd None: a member's relative redirection and tee target are refused ("cannot follow"). Spud's are skipped, unchanged. An absolute target is checked for both. Pinned; proposal 29.
7. Subshell `(cd x)`, `$(cd x)`, backticks, `<(cd x)`, `sh -c` and `bash -c`, background `cd x &`: no move (probe: pwd unchanged). A redirection inside the subshell after its cd is checked there.
8. Pipeline: non-last elements never move in either shell, including `{ cd; } | cat`. The last element moves in zsh (current shell) but not bash (subshell): probe `true | cd /tmp; pwd` gives /tmp in zsh, base in bash. Both directories are checked.
9. CDPATH: a bare relative target (not /, ./, ../) is checked under every entry and the current directory. Probe: bash tries CDPATH first, zsh ./ first; both use CDPATH when ./ has no match. Sources, in order: a prefix or earlier assignment, export/declare, zsh's cdpath=(...), else the hook's inherited environment. A value holding `$`, or CDPATH+=, is None. Limit: a CDPATH set only in the user's zsh profile and not exported to Claude Code is invisible; this machine's Bash tool has none.
10. zsh `cd old new`: zsh replaces the first occurrence in PWD (probe: aa/aa/x becomes bb/aa/x); bash 3.2 changes to the first argument and a later bash stays. All three are checked. Three or more arguments: None.
11. Tildes: ~ and ~/x expand to HOME. ~+ and ~+/x are the current candidates (probe: same as PWD in both), for cd and for redirection targets. ~-, ~N and ~name are None (zsh named directories: `hash -d nd=/tmp; cd ~nd` goes to /tmp). Globs and brace lists in a cd target are None.

Found and fixed in the same family, each with red tests:
- `ls<newline>git push`: newline was not a separator.
- `ls # don't<newline>git push`: shlex's comment ate the next line.
- `(true)>ledger/...`: the redirection was lost.
- `cat <(git push)`: hidden.
- `timeout -s KILL 5`, `env -u X`, `exec -a n`, `ionice -c 3`, `xargs -J %`, `caffeinate -t 5`, `stdbuf -o 0`, `sudo -Eu root`, `script -q file`, `time -o f` hid the command word.
- A cd that may not run (after && or ||; in if, case, loop or function bodies; every branch kept) or may fail (target not existing now) leaves both directories for what follows its and-or list; what follows `cd x &&` is in x.
- A relative cd in a loop or function body, and source or `.`, are None.
- A compound command's redirections are checked where it started.

**Tests, red first.** BashHookCase extracted from PreBashTest. ShellModelTest has 10 methods with subtests covering the ticket's five evidence commands (for a ** member, the tests/** lead, and Spud), lower, upper, mixed and /usr/bin/UPPER spellings of all 20 wrappers before a push, value options, and every case above. Controls stay silent: `cd <outside> && echo x > rel` for a member, `ENV FOO=1 ls`, `NOHUP git status`, `TIMEOUT 5 git log`, `COMMAND -v git`, a status with a comment naming a push, a quoted newline, a backslash-newline, `$((1 + 2))`, `ls *(.)`, `arr=()`. `pushd home && spud member log` is still allowed. `CD home && spud ...` is now silent (CD is a program). Final test file against a scratchpad copy of the unchanged bin/: 10 of 10 methods fail, 147 failures counting subtests. Now the whole suite from the worktree: Ran 460 tests in 169.433s, OK (450 before).

**Proposals filed:** 29 (P3), Spud's relative redirection after an unfollowable directory is unchecked. 30 (P2), a glob in a redirection target expands in zsh and bash -c (probe overwrote ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md via ledg*/tickets/SPD-00?.md) while the hook checks the literal path.
